did.abstract: Morton N. Cohen (1921–2017) was a scholar whose career centered on the life and work of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, better known as Lewis Carroll. Cohen is known for co-editing The Letters of Lewis Carroll (1979) with Roger Lancelyn Green, his book Lewis Carroll: A Biography (1995), and numerous other essays, articles, books, and lectures on the subject. The Morton N. Cohen Papers (1840s–2015) document this decades-long scholarly pursuit through writing drafts, editorial materials, and extensive research and subject files used across all of his writing projects, as well as materials reflecting his active participation in the Carroll scholarly community, including original Dodgson letters dating between 1872-1896 and ephemera collected over the years. Also included in this collection are professional correspondence with individuals and institutions central to Carroll scholarship and the rare books world, teaching files from The City College of New York, manuscripts for novels written under the pseudonym John Moreton, and research and writing on other literary figures including Rudyard Kipling and H. Rider Haggard. A modest amount of personal material rounds out the collection including college class notes, correspondence, and ephemera related to Cohen and his long-time partner, Richard (Dick) Swift (1924-2002).

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Transferred by the estate of Morton N. Cohen in 2003 and 2018; the accession numbers associated with these gifts are 2003.129, 2018.114, and 2018.122.

appraisal.head: Appraisal
appraisal.p: The following items were separated from the collection during processing (12 containers): duplicates of Lewis Carroll/Macmillan letters in the form of 4 microfilm reels and enlarged photocopies; large, rolled photocopies of Carroll letters; general information material from research institutions; student letters of recommendation, graded papers, and evaluations; medical records and bills; water damaged duplicated material from research institutions; metal sculpture of man writing; and duplicate copies of press clippings, publications, and photographs.

bioghist.head: Biographical Note
bioghist.p:
Morton N. Cohen (1921–2017) was a literary scholar and biographer whose career centered on the life and work of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, better known as Lewis Carroll. He received his MA from Columbia University in 1950, and went on to teach English literature at The City College of New York, where he remained for much of his academic career.
Cohen's scholarly output on Carroll was substantial and wide-ranging. His editorial work produced several publications, including The Letters of Lewis Carroll (1979), co-edited with Roger Lancelyn Green; and Lewis Carroll and House of Macmillan (2007), co-edited with Anita Gandolfo. His most significant contribution to the field was Lewis Carroll: A Biography (1995), the first major biography of Dodgson in decades, which drew on a lifetime of research. Alongside these works, Cohen produced numerous essays, articles, and lectures on Carroll throughout his career and was an active participant in Carroll scholarly societies and communities.
Cohen shared his personal life with his long-time partner, Richard (Dick) Swift, who predeceased him in 2002.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Material was removed from their original folders and envelopes and rehoused into acid free folders and boxes. Subject files retain their original titles and in some cases the original envelopes are included in the files. All material was unfolded when possible. Oversized material was unfolded and placed in appropriate housing. Original letters written by Charles L. Dodgson, Rudyard Kipling, and Rider Haggard were listed at the item level in the inventory. A note regarding the existence of nude photographs of children taken by Dodgson was added at the collection, subseries, and item level. Conservators individually foldered original letters and treated a selection of folded proofs, creating appropriate storage for fragile material.

A selection of Cohen's books (82 total) were separated from his papers and designated for bibliographic treatment. Loose material from these books was removed and stored along with a copy of the title page of the book it was pulled from as part of the archival collection. A spreadsheet listing the separated book titles was created and stored in the curator's collection files. Nine books were retained in the collection.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
The Morton N. Cohen Papers (1840s–2015) document the decades-long scholarly career of Morton N. Cohen, a Lewis Carroll scholar, through his writings, research files, and personal materials. The collection offers a view into the research, editorial, and intellectual processes behind a scholar and writer; the broader world of Carroll studies and collecting; and Cohen's personal life.
The bulk of the collection relates to Cohen's writings on Lewis Carroll and Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, spanning in date from the 1960s to the mid-2010s, and documents his publications from early research and outreach through multiple stages of editing. Of particular note are the files for The Letters of Lewis Carroll (1979), for which Cohen and his co-editor Roger Lancelyn Green conducted an extensive search to locate Carroll letters; and Lewis Carroll: A Biography (1995), represented by edited drafts and proofs. Essays, articles, speeches, and lectures produced concurrently throughout his career reflect his engagement with Carroll scholarship beyond his book-length works. Cohen's research and subject files were accumulated over several decades and drawn upon across all of his writing projects. The files reflect the wide range of his Carroll research interests, including friendships with children, photography, and mathematical writings. These files typically contain press clippings, notes, and correspondence. Of particular note are Carroll's transcribed diary entries and annotated copies of Carroll's letters spanning the 1840s through 1898. Some of these files contain reproductions of nude photographs of children by Charles L. Dodgson, retained for their historical and scholarly significance as documents of his photographic practice and Victorian visual culture. Cohen's participation within the broader Carroll studies community is documented through society materials, commemorative event programs, and ephemera, as well as a small number of original letters and items purchased by Cohen, including several written by Dodgson to various correspondents between 1872 and 1896.
The collection also documents Cohen's career through his correspondence, teaching materials, and writings not directly related to his Carroll scholarship. Highlights include manuscripts for several novels written under Cohen's pseudonym John Moreton, teaching notes from The City College of New York, and research and writing on Rudyard Kipling and H. Rider Haggard.

did.unittitle: Series I. Writings on Lewis Carroll / Charles L. Dodgson

physdesc.extent: in 35 manuscript boxes, 4 oversize flat boxes, 1 flat-file folder, and 7 folders in shared boxes

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This series contains materials related to Morton Cohen's writings on Lewis Carroll/Charles L. Dodgson, representing a majority of his scholarly output on this subject. The series documents the communications, editorial, and production history of Cohen's book projects, published between 1979 to 2007, as well as his essays, articles, speeches, and lectures produced concurrently throughout his career.
The books subseries offer a view into Cohen's working methods as a scholar and editor, tracing each publication from early research and outreach through multiple stages of drafting, editing, and proof correction. The essays and articles subseries reflects his engagement with Carroll scholarship beyond his book-length works, while the speeches and lectures subseries complements this material by documenting his active life as a public scholar and speaker.

did.unittitle: Subseries I.A. The Letters of Lewis Carroll (1979)

physdesc.extent: in 9 manuscript boxes, 4 oversize flat boxes, 1 flat-file folder, and 5 folders in shared boxes

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This subseries documents the research, editorial, and production history of The Letters of Lewis Carroll (1979), edited by Cohen and Roger Lancelyn Green, and offers a detailed view into the work of assembling and editing a scholarly edition of primary correspondence.
The subseries contains material on the research and outreach phase of the project, including form letters sent during the 1960s and 1970s to institutions and individuals inquiring whether they held Carroll letters, followed by the resulting correspondence. Correspondence related to the sourcing and rights of images and illustrations for the volumes is also present, along with a notebook used to track the book's illustrations throughout the production process.
The editorial and production process during the 1970s is documented through multiple stages of proofs, including edited galley proofs, an edited copy of galley proofs incorporating image page mock-ups, mock-up pages, and notes tracking the status of proof corrections. Comments on the manuscript from various readers and colleagues are also included, as is a funding report related to the project.
Post-publication materials include correspondence related to corrections from the general public and other scholars, as well as book reviews and related press coverage. A small amount of material related to the subsequent, related publication of Lewis Carroll and The Kitchins (1980) is also in this subseries, including Carroll letter copies and related notes.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries documents the research and editorial work behind The Russian Journal--II: A Record Kept by Henry Parry Liddon of a Tour Taken with C.L. Research notes and an edited early manuscript reflect the initial work, followed by subsequent drafts, notes, and corrections documenting the later stages of Cohen's editing. did.unittitle: Subseries I.C. Lewis Carroll: Interviews and Recollections (1989)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries documents the research, editorial, and permissions work behind Lewis Carroll: Interviews and Recollections (1989), an anthology edited by Cohen that accumulated firsthand accounts of Lewis Carroll by those who knew him. Correspondence, notes, and research materials document the process of identifying and assembling the book, while a substantial amount of use permissions document the rights clearance process involved in reprinting previously published material. The subseries also contains edited proof pages and a draft index, representing the final stages of the book's production.

did.unittitle: Edited Proof Pages and Draft Index
Subseries I.D. Lewis Carroll: A Biography (1995)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This subseries documents the research, writing, and production of Lewis Carroll: A Biography (1995). This subseries offers a detailed view into the creation of a literary biography written by Cohen.
The research and writing phase is represented through introduction and chapter files containing notes, correspondence, and research materials, as well as general research files. A collection of images and illustrations, the majority of which were not ultimately used in the published work, is also in this subseries, along with correspondence and a list of editing notes and comments from readers and colleagues.
The editorial and production process is well documented, tracing the book through multiple editing stages. Notated drafts of chapters and appendix materials, as well as edited cuts and paste-ups reflecting the physical production methods, are in this subseries. The subseries also includes a full sequence of galley proof stages: a first pass, a revised first pass, a second pass, and a third pass, each edited and annotated. Also included is a final review of the manuscript by someone identified as Peter, and a separate final read by Cohen, which together offer a view into the final editorial process. An edited illustrations list and index, as well as corrections and proof edits, round out the production materials. Post-publication materials include press reviews and correspondence related to corrections following publication.

physdesc.extent: in 5 manuscript boxes and 1 oversize flat box

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This subseries documents the research and production of Lewis Carroll and House of Macmillan (2007), co-edited by Cohen and Anita Gandolfo. A substantial number of files in the subseries contain notated copies of original and transcribed Carroll letters dating from 1832 to 1897, which were the primary resources used in the book.
Notes and other research materials document the process, while correspondence with Cambridge University Press and Gandolfo illuminate both the publishing relationship and the collaborative editorial work for this book. The production of the book is documented through edited manuscripts, a draft index, and page proofs, tracing the work from draft through final production stages.

physdesc.extent: in 4 manuscript boxes, 1 oversize flat box, and 1 folder in a shared box

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This subseries contains essays and articles on Lewis Carroll/Charles L. Dodgson written by Cohen throughout his career, produced during the same time as his book projects. These short pieces reflect the full range of Cohen's scholarly interests and engagement with Carroll studies over several decades and demonstrate the breadth of his contribution to the field beyond his book-length works.
Cohen's essays and articles address a variety of subjects within Carroll scholarship including Carroll's photography, most notably his nude photographs of children; his relationships with children; his educational and technological interests; and his place within Victorian children's literature authors. Several of these pieces refer to Alice's Adventures in Wonderland and its cultural significance, including psychoanalytic readings, and theatrical and musical adaptations. Two radio scripts where Cohen discusses his work are also in this subseries.
Of particular note are the files related to a booklet marking the 100th anniversary of Dodgson's death, Reflections on a Looking Glass: A Centennial Celebration of Lewis Carroll, Photographer. Work files include correspondence, images, layout boards, proofs, and essays, which document Cohen's role in the publication.
These files contain reproductions of nude photographs of children by Charles L. Dodgson (Lewis Carroll), retained for their historical and scholarly significance as documents of his photographic practice and Victorian visual culture.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This subseries contains materials related to speeches and lectures delivered by Cohen, dating from the 1960s to the early 2000s, and reflecting his active role as a public scholar and speaker within Lewis Carroll studies. The materials document his engagements at academic conferences and university settings, as well as book parties and club gatherings.
The lectures and speeches address recurring themes in Cohen's scholarship, including Carroll's morality, his relationships with women and children, his photography, and his place within Victorian culture and literature. Several titles appear in multiple versions, most notably "Reeling and Writhing with Lewis Carroll," which exists in numerous iterations and presentations over the years. Also of significance are materials related to lectures over the years for The Alfred C. Berol Collection of Lewis Carroll located within the New York University's Fales Library & Special Collections. An NYU-produced audio recording of Cohen reading a chapter from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is also in this subseries.

Series II. Carroll Research and Subject Files

physdesc.extent: in 31 manuscript boxes and 1 oversize flat box

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This series contains material accumulated by Cohen over several decades of scholarly research on Charles L. Dodgson/Lewis Carroll, drawn upon by Cohen for all of his writing projects. Original folder titles were retained wherever possible and reflect the breadth of Cohen's research interests: people, subjects, resources, and objects. The dates of material within the files range from the 1840s to 2007, and typically contain a mix of press clippings, articles, copies of published and unpublished sources, Cohen's handwritten and typed notes, correspondence, event announcements, and auction catalogue clippings. Manuscripts from Cohen's own writings are often interfiled within the relevant subject folder.
These files document Cohen's research into Carroll's life and relationships, including friendships with children and their families, his correspondence, photography, and more sensitive biographical subjects such as nudity, sexuality, and psychology. Individual files are dedicated to many of Carroll's child friends and their families, among them the Bowmans, the Liddells, the Kitchins, the Chataway family, the Rix family, the Standen family, and others, and typically contain correspondence, notes, genealogical information, press clippings, and photocopies of primary sources.
Carroll's creative and intellectual output is represented in this series with files accumulated on specific literary works including Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Sylvie and Bruno, and The Snark, as well as his mathematical and logical writings, his work as a photographer, his drawings, and his letters to editors. Files on specific themes in Carroll's work and biography include dreams, imagination, morality, religion, love, marriage, and Victorian culture.
The series also documents Cohen's extensive use of archival and special collections at institutions including the Bodleian Library, Huntington Library, Morgan Library, Harvard Library, and New York Public Library, among others. Auction catalogues and ephemera purchase records throughout the research and subject files reflect Cohen's active engagement with the Carroll rare materials market over the years.
Of particular note are several files of transcribed and annotated copies of Lewis Carroll's letters, spanning the 1840s through 1898, as well as typescripts of Carroll's diary entries which were transcribed by Carroll's niece and originally given to Carroll scholar Roger Lancelyn Green during the preparation of his edition of the diaries. Copies of these diary transcriptions were given to Cohen by Green.
Research subject notecards and files titled "Sources to Consult" and "Raw Material" offer a view into Cohen's working methods as a scholar. Essays and writings on Carroll by other scholars in these files indicate Cohen's desire to track the output of published works within the Carroll scholarly community.
This series contains reproductions of nude photographs of children by Charles L. Dodgson, retained for their historical and scholarly significance as documents of his photographic practice and Victorian visual culture.

Series III. Lewis Carroll Original Letters, Collected Ephemera, and Carroll Societies

physdesc.extent: in 4 manuscript boxes and 1 oversize flat box

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This series contains material related to both Cohen's participation in Carroll scholarly communities and his role as a collector of Carroll ephemera.
The series contains a collection of original letters and items written by Charles L. Dodgson between 1871-1897 to various correspondents and purchased by Cohen. A small number of letters written by others but related to Dodgson include those of illustrators Harry Furniss and Henry Holiday. Other items of Carroll ephemera collected by Cohen in this series include 1890s postage stamp cases and Royal Mail postage stamps containing Alice's Adventures in Wonderland illustrations, as well as various periodicals and advertisements highlighting the book and its characters. There are also Tristan da Cunha postage stamps depicting the Dodgson family. This series also contains the loose items found within books from Cohen's personal library, along with photocopies of the book title pages to provide bibliographical context. These loose items include ticket stubs, bookseller bookmarks, personal letters, and purchase receipts, which offer a glimpse into Cohen's personal life and collecting habits.
The series also contains material documenting Carroll-related events and exhibitions, reflecting the broader cultural life surrounding Carroll studies. These include programs and promotional materials for Alice's Adventures in Wonderland-themed plays and productions; materials related to the Morgan Library exhibition Lewis Carroll and Alice, 1832–1982; events marking Carroll's 150th birthday; the 100th anniversary of Carroll's death; and various other exhibitions and commemorative events.
Cohen's involvement with various Lewis Carroll societies is documented through printed material, correspondence, and meeting notes related to the Lewis Carroll Society of the United Kingdom, the Lewis Carroll Society of North America, the Lewis Carroll Society of Australia, the Lewis Carroll Society Publication Trust, and the Lewis Carroll Birthplace Trust.

Series IV. Literary Writing Projects and Professional Materials

physdesc.extent: in 8 manuscript boxes and 1 half manuscript box

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This series contains Cohen's professional correspondence, teaching materials, and writings not directly related to his Lewis Carroll scholarship, though Carroll-related matters appear throughout correspondence files, reflecting the degree to which his Carroll work permeated his broader professional life.
Cohen's teaching career is represented through course materials from The City College, including syllabi, notes, and research for a biography course and a children's literature course, as well as documentation on his sabbatical leave and employment records. A curriculum vitae and funding files for various projects are also in this series.
A substantial amount of professional correspondence is in this series, with individuals and institutions related to Carroll scholarship and the rare books world, including Roger Lancelyn Green, Martin Gardner, Selwyn Goodacre, Edward Guiliano, and Anita Gandolfo, among others, as well as correspondence with institutions including Christ Church (University of Oxford), Oxford University Press, Princeton University Library, the New York Public Library, the Rosenbach Museum and Library, and Yale University Library. Several folders of general correspondence organized by decade are also in this series. Researchers should note that correspondence can be found throughout this collection and is not limited to this series, including individual book project files in Series I, letters interfiled within the research and subject files of Series II, and within the personal materials of Series V.
Cohen's work as a novelist is documented through manuscripts and related materials for several works of fiction, including two novels written under the pseudonym John Moreton. Also in this series are materials related to Cohen's research and writing on other literary figures, including essays and draft materials on Rudyard Kipling and H. Rider Haggard, as well as class notes and papers on Upton Sinclair.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
This series contains material related to the personal life of Morton N. Cohen and his long-time partner, Richard (Dick) Swift. Materials documenting Cohen and Swift's life together include notes and letters addressed to them as a couple, among them correspondence from fellow Carroll scholar and friend Roger Lancelyn Green and his wife June. The couple's friendship with author Shirley Hazzard is reflected through the handwritten inscriptions in each book in this series, as well as the loose items placed within which include notes, letters, Hazzard's wedding invitation, and reviews of her work.
This series contains the couple's estate planning instructions and address books, as well as material related to artist Martin Hardie including artwork purchase records, catalogues, and press clippings.
Materials belonging individually to Cohen and Swift are also present in this series. Cohen's early academic life is represented through class notes and coursework from the 1940s–1950s, reflecting the foundation of his scholarly career, alongside a small collection of correspondence from friends and family. Swift's baby book from 1924 and a selection of his professional and personal correspondence are also included.
